channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: New Kia Model Production to Begin in Jizzakh, Uzbekistan
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev attended the launch ceremony for joint projects with leading South Korean companies and financial institutions in Jizzakh. Production of a new Kia model is set to commence in the region, signaling a significant step in automotive manufacturing collaboration.

item.title: Uzbekistan and South Korea May Establish Industrial-Technological Alliance
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev and South Korean Prime Minister Han Duck-soo opened a joint business forum. Over 300 representatives from government and business circles attended, including leaders from major Korean companies like Lotte Chemical and Hyundai Motor Group. The forum highlighted opportunities for increased trade and investment.

item.title: Uzbekneftgaz Prepares for Winter Season, Focuses on Gas Production and Supply
item.description: Uzbekneftgaz has begun a 30-day preparation phase for the autumn-winter season, focusing on gas extraction, well conditions, and stable supply. Despite significant efforts, some indicators remain below expectations. The company emphasizes the need for direct action at fields and wells to ensure gas availability for the public.

item.title: Chyngyz Akhmatov Appointed First Deputy Prosecutor General of Kyrgyzstan
item.description: Chyngyz Akhmatov has been appointed First Deputy Prosecutor General of Kyrgyzstan. He was introduced to the staff today. Akhmatov has worked in the prosecutor's office since 2004 and previously served as the Prosecutor of Osh region until his recent appointment.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Completes Construction and Renovation of 81 Schools for New Academic Year
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has completed the construction and renovation of 81 schools by the 2026-2027 academic year, according to the Ministry of Construction. Forty schools were built from scratch, and 41 underwent major renovations. Additional schools are nearing completion across various regions.

item.title: NABU to Assist Kyrgyzstan in Updating Red Book of Endangered Species
item.description: The German Nature and Biodiversity Conservation Union (NABU) will help Kyrgyzstan update its Red Book of Endangered Species. The project, funded with 21 million soms over 24 months, will use modern scientific data to assess rare species populations and threats.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Competition Committee Investigates WB Taxi Over Passenger Complaints
item.description: Uzbekistan's Committee for the Development of Competition and Protection of Consumer Rights has sent an inquiry to WB Taxi due to numerous passenger complaints. The committee noted an increase in complaints regarding taxi services, with nearly 20 related to WB Taxi reported between January and August. Issues include cars not arriving and lack of operator response.

item.title: One Kilogram of Psychotropic Substance Seized from Child's Electric Car in Bishkek
item.description: Kyrgyzstan authorities, with Russian cooperation, have intercepted a supply of psychotropic substances from Russia to Bishkek. A 20-year-old suspect was detained in Bishkek with a one-kilogram briquette of Alpha-PVP found in a child's electric car. The operation prevented the distribution of over 4,200 doses, with potential proceeds exceeding 4.5 million soms.

item.title: Turkic states' muftis adopt fatwa on artificial intelligence use
item.description: The 7th Meeting of the Council of Heads of Muslim Religious Boards of the Organization of Turkic States (OTS) in Baku resulted in the adoption of six fatwas, including one on the use of artificial intelligence in issuing religious rulings. Joint statements were also signed on family protection, Islam's stance on science and technology, and takfir.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Faces Potential Gasoline Shortages Due to Russian Supply Issues
item.description: Kyrgyzstan, heavily reliant on Russian gasoline imports, may face shortages. Russia is the primary supplier from the EAEU, accounting for 99% of Kyrgyzstan's imports in early 2026. Potential reductions or irregular supplies from Russia, due to domestic issues and export bans, could impact Kyrgyzstan's fuel availability despite EAEU exemptions.

item.title: Uzbek President Meets with Speaker of South Korean National Assembly
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev met with Speaker of the South Korean National Assembly Cho Jung-sik during a state visit. They emphasized the role of parliaments in advancing the strategic partnership, noting active inter-parliamentary groups and exchanges. Discussions also covered enhancing economic, investment, and cultural ties, and establishing parliamentary monitoring mechanisms.

item.title: CSTO Considers Resuming Cooperation with OSCE, Open to Dialogue with NATO
item.description: The CSTO sees value in resuming cooperation with the OSCE, with Secretary General Taalatbek Masadykov meeting his OSCE counterpart. The organization also remains open to dialogue with NATO, despite previous unsuccessful attempts. The CSTO prioritizes cooperation with traditional partners like the UN and SCO, while developing relations with new blocs.

item.title: Russian Drone Attack on Kyiv and Regions Kills One, Wounds Several
item.description: On September 15, 2026, Russian drones struck gas stations and warehouses in Kyiv, resulting in seven injuries, one of whom later died. Attacks also hit civilian infrastructure in Odesa region. Ukraine's air defense reportedly shot down 187 of 200 drones used.

item.title: Tajikistan Holds First Secretariat Meeting of Digital Coordination Council
item.description: The first meeting of the Digital Coordination Council's secretariat in Tajikistan's communications sector took place on September 11, 2026. The secretariat aims to fulfill presidential directives and implement the 2040 communications development strategy.

item.title: Uzbekistan and South Korea aim to build industrial-technological alliance
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev proposed expanding cooperation with South Korea in industrial cooperation, energy, transport, digitalization, and artificial intelligence. He invited Korean businesses to invest in building new production capacities and developing technologies in Uzbekistan, aiming to transform the country into a key regional production and export hub.

item.title: Kazakhstan denies asylum to Chechen activist Mansur Movlayev
item.description: Kazakhstan's Court of Cassation for Administrative Cases upheld previous decisions denying refugee status to Chechen activist Mansur Movlayev. The court's ruling means Movlayev will not be granted asylum in Kazakhstan, following the decisions of lower instances.

item.title: Uzbekistan and South Korea may form industrial-technological alliance
item.description: Uzbekistan and South Korea could form an industrial-technological alliance. President Shavkat Mirziyoyev proposed expanding cooperation in industrial cooperation, energy, transport, digitalization, and artificial intelligence during a joint business forum. He invited Korean companies to invest in building new production capacities and developing technologies in Uzbekistan.

item.title: Tajikistan and UK to expand cooperation in emergency prevention
item.description: Tajikistan's Committee for Emergency Situations and Civil Defense met with the UK Ambassador to discuss a new cooperation agreement and joint projects. Discussions focused on emergency prevention, disaster risk reduction, and enhancing rescue services' capabilities, including training and equipment.

item.title: Uzbekistan and South Korea to expand cooperation in processing critical minerals
item.description: Uzbekistan and South Korea will enhance their collaboration in processing critical minerals. President Shavkat Mirziyoyev also discussed partnership prospects in technologies, transport, and cybersecurity with the Prime Minister of South Korea.

item.title: Uzbekistan mandates drug testing for military conscripts and contract soldiers
item.description: Uzbekistan has established a procedure for mandatory drug testing for individuals called up for compulsory military service and those joining on contract. The testing involves a two-stage process, including express tests and mass spectrometry analysis, to detect narcotic substances.

item.title: International Forum 'Taj Tech – 2026' to be Held in Dushanbe
item.description: Dushanbe will host the 'Taj Tech – 2026' International Forum on September 29-30. The event will focus on digital transformation, AI, innovation, startup ecosystems, digital infrastructure, and international tech cooperation. It aims to showcase Tajikistan's innovation potential, aligning with President Emomali Rahmon's initiative for digital economy development.

item.title: Kazakhstan's QazETA System Not Mandatory for Kyrgyz Citizens Yet
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs clarified that the QazETA system is not mandatory for Kyrgyz citizens entering Kazakhstan, as it is currently in a pilot phase. Entry procedures remain unchanged. Citizens will be informed if migration rules are officially altered by Kazakhstan.

item.title: ROX Group plans $1.5 billion investment for Uchtepa City project in Tashkent
item.description: Vietnam's ROX Group plans to invest $1.5 billion in Uzbekistan, focusing on real estate, energy, finance, and tourism. A key project is the development of Uchtepa City in Tashkent, a 37-hectare complex featuring modern business centers, residences, and new infrastructure.

item.title: CSTO Sees Value in Resuming Dialogue with OSCE, Secretary General Says
item.description: The CSTO sees merit in resuming cooperation with the OSCE, according to Secretary General Talatbek Masadikov. He met with the OSCE Secretary General in May, noting a mutual desire for dialogue. Masadikov also addressed potential engagement with NATO, stating the CSTO remains committed to a pragmatic approach despite past unsuccessful attempts at dialogue.

item.title: UN Reports Record High in International Remittances to Low and Middle-Income Countries
item.description: International remittances to low and middle-income countries are projected to reach a record $728.6 billion in 2025, according to a UN report. This figure significantly surpasses official development assistance and foreign direct investment. Remittances have become a stable and crucial funding source for households, aiding in covering basic needs and future investments.

item.title: Saida Mirziyoyeva Presented with Major Architectural Projects in Tashkent
item.description: Saida Mirziyoyeva, head of the Presidential Administration, met with initiators of major architectural projects, urban planners, and specialists in Tashkent. She emphasized the need for careful consideration of urban development, infrastructure, and ecological balance as the city expands. The goal is to make Tashkent more comfortable and safe.

item.title: Kyrgyz Prosecutor General's Office reviews complaint regarding Kamchybek Tashiev's case
item.description: The Prosecutor General's Office of Kyrgyzstan has registered and begun reviewing a complaint filed by the lawyer of former GKNB head Kamchybek Tashiev. The lawyer alleges that Tashiev and seven others were convicted under a new charge not previously presented, hindering their defense. The Bishkek City Court reclassified the charge to obstructing electoral rights.

item.title: Uzbekistan welcomed over 9 million foreign tourists in January-August
item.description: In the first eight months of 2026, Uzbekistan received 9.1 million foreign visitors, a 21.1% increase compared to the same period last year. The National Statistics Committee reported that the majority of tourists came from Kyrgyzstan, followed by Kazakhstan and Tajikistan. Other significant visitor groups originated from Russia, Afghanistan, China, and Turkmenistan.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan to commission over 100 educational facilities in 2026
item.description: Kyrgyzstan plans to open more than 100 educational facilities in 2026, according to the Ministry of Education. This includes 34 schools and 28 kindergartens commissioned on September 11, and an additional 58 facilities, mostly new schools and kindergartens, by year-end. This initiative addresses the issue of dilapidated school buildings across the country.

item.title: Kyrgyz MP questions procurement of hybrid cars for water ministry
item.description: A Member of Parliament in Kyrgyzstan, Ulan Bakasov, questioned the necessity of purchasing three hybrid cars for the Ministry of Water Resources, Agriculture, and Processing Industry. He cited media reports about the tender and asked for justification, noting that such vehicles might not be suitable for developing water management. The deputy minister stated the purchase is part of a World Bank project.

item.title: Campaign for Eco-Friendly Bags Launched in Dushanbe
item.description: A campaign promoting the use of eco-friendly bags has started in Dushanbe, Tajikistan. Launched by the Environmental Protection Committee, it aims to support the country's green economy strategy and raise public environmental awareness.

item.title: Tajik President Emomali Rahmon Travels to Seoul for Central Asia-Korea Summit
item.description: Tajik President Emomali Rahmon has departed for Seoul to attend the first Central Asia-South Korea summit. The meeting aims to foster cooperation between the regions.

item.title: CSTO Secretary General suggests dialogue with NATO is possible
item.description: The Secretary General of the Collective Security Treaty Organization (CSTO), Talantbek Masadikov, stated that the organization does not rule out the possibility of developing dialogue with NATO. He noted that CSTO remains committed to a pragmatic approach despite past unsuccessful dialogue attempts. Masadikov also expressed concern over NATO's rhetoric and military infrastructure near CSTO responsibility zones.

item.title: Tajikistan to issue electronic vehicle inspection certificates via eKhizmat.tj portal
item.description: Starting September 15, Tajikistan will issue electronic vehicle inspection certificates exclusively through the eKhizmat.tj state services portal. The physical inspection process remains unchanged, conducted at diagnostic centers. The portal will only handle the final electronic certificate issuance within 30 days of inspection.

item.title: Tajik President Emomali Rahmon begins official visit to South Korea for summit
item.description: Tajikistan's President Emomali Rahmon has departed for the Republic of Korea for an official visit and to attend the "Central Asia – Republic of Korea" Summit. He was seen off at Dushanbe International Airport by high-ranking officials. The delegation includes ministers of foreign affairs, economic development, education, energy, water resources, and the head of the National Bank.

item.title: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev meets with Speaker of the Korean National Assembly
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev met with Speaker Cho Joo-sik of the Korean National Assembly during his state visit to South Korea. They discussed strengthening strategic partnership, parliamentary cooperation, and implementing agreements in trade, investment, and cultural-humanitarian spheres.

item.title: US sanctions on Iran could impact Dushanbe-Tehran relations, media reports
item.description: A US media outlet suggests new US sanctions against Iran may affect relations between Dushanbe and Tehran. The sanctions are expected to impact the transport of goods and fuel, banking operations, and trade turnover.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Competition Committee Launches Case Against Regional Power Grid
item.description: Uzbekistan's Competition Development and Consumer Rights Protection Committee has initiated proceedings against regional power grid companies for unlawfully collecting 5.5 billion soms from entrepreneurs. These charges relate to fees for reconnecting electricity supply after debt settlement, which were abolished by presidential decree and government resolutions.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Establishes Waste Recycling Registry to Promote Circular Economy
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Natural Resources is creating a digital registry for waste recyclers to support sustainable development and producer responsibility. Officials are inspecting companies processing paper, plastic, and textiles. The ministry urges recyclers to obtain licenses to avoid penalties.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan to Install 44,000 Smart Electricity Meters in Toktogul and Nooken Districts
item.description: Kyrgyzstan plans to install 44,000 smart electricity meters in Toktogul and Nooken districts by 2026 as part of an automated metering system. Since 2024, 106,000 meters have been installed in the Jalal-Abad region. The system aims for accurate consumption tracking and efficient grid management.
